excerpt: Pass Designer is Apple's free beta Mac app for designing Apple Wallet passes and previewing them exactly as iPhone and Apple Watch show them. Requirements, what it does and alternatives.
content:
Pass Designer is a Mac app from Apple for designing Apple Wallet passes, such as boarding passes, event tickets, coupons, store cards and membership cards. You start from one of Apple's templates or your own design, and a live preview shows the pass exactly as it will appear on iPhone and Apple Watch, using the same rendering as iOS and watchOS.

It covers six pass styles, including the new poster-style generic pass, and generates eight barcode types, from QR and PDF417 to EAN-13. You can edit colours and fields, add images at the sizes each pass needs, and edit the semantic tags that let Siri Suggestions, Calendar and Maps understand a boarding pass or event ticket. It validates your pass as you work, flagging missing keys, and can build a backward-compatible version for older iOS releases.

Pass Designer saves a pass template, not a finished pass. To give a pass to customers, you sign it with an Apple-issued certificate from an Apple developer account, using Apple's Pass Builder package or by hand. Apple introduced Pass Designer at WWDC26 and still labels it a beta. It appeared on Product Hunt on 4 October 2026, under Apple's product page, with 112 upvotes.

We have not tested Pass Designer ourselves. This page brings together Apple's product page, documentation and WWDC session, its Product Hunt listing and the official pages of comparable services, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.os: macOS 27 or later; Apple Account sign-in to download
profile.summary_short: Apple's free beta Mac app for designing and previewing Apple Wallet passes
use_cases: Designing a boarding pass, event ticket, coupon, store card or membership card for Apple Wallet
Previewing exactly how a pass will look on iPhone and Apple Watch before you ship it
Adding semantic tags so Siri Suggestions, Calendar and Maps can use a boarding pass or ticket
Checking a pass for missing or unexpected fields before signing it

fit: are a developer or designer building Apple Wallet passes for an airline, venue, shop or membership scheme
already have, or can get, access to an Apple developer account with a Pass Type ID certificate
want an accurate preview without writing pass JSON by hand
not_fit: need Google Wallet or Samsung Wallet passes too: Pass Designer is for Apple Wallet only (PassKit, Passcreator and Pass2U cover several wallets)
want a hosted service that issues and updates passes for you: Pass Designer only designs templates

pricing.intro: Pass Designer is a free download from Apple's developer site. Apple does not state a price for the tool.

plans.name: Beta
plans.detail: Sign in with an Apple Account; if prompted, complete the free registration and accept the Apple Developer Agreement

notes: Distributing real passes requires signing them with an Apple-issued certificate tied to an Apple developer account. Creating that certificate needs the Account Holder or Admin role. Check Apple's developer programme page for membership costs.
Pass Designer saves a .pkpasstemplate bundle, which is not a signed pass. Signing is done with Apple's Pass Builder package or manually.

alternatives.intro: Product Hunt lists no alternatives for this launch. These are services that also create Apple Wallet passes; prices are what each one's own pricing page states, checked on 14 October 2026.

items.name: PassKit
items.what: Hosted platform for creating, issuing and updating Apple Wallet and Google Wallet passes
items.starts_at: Platform fee plus pass volume; see its pricing page
items.difference: Hosts, issues and updates passes and supports Google Wallet. Pass Designer is a free design tool for Apple Wallet only.

items.name: Passcreator
items.what: Web service for loyalty cards, tickets, gift and membership cards on Apple, Google and Samsung Wallet
items.starts_at: Free plan with 5 active registrations; paid tiers via its pricing page
items.difference: Web-based, works across three wallets and bills by passes saved to devices.

items.name: Pass2U
items.what: Create, distribute and update wallet passes with loyalty, redemption and analytics
items.starts_at: 50 free credits; pay-as-you-go from $50 for 8,000 credits; Premium from $39/month
items.difference: Hosted distribution billed by credits or active passes.

pros: Preview uses the same rendering as iOS and watchOS
Validation flags missing or unexpected pass fields as you work
Semantic tags editable without code, with automatic backward-compatible versions
Generates eight barcode types in the app
cons: Still a beta, and needs macOS 27 or later
Produces unsigned templates; signing and distribution need a developer account and separate tooling
No hosting, issuing or updating of passes

x.none: We found no posts about Pass Designer on X to link yet.

faq.a: Yes. It is a free beta download from Apple's developer site; you sign in with an Apple Account and accept the Apple Developer Agreement if prompted.

faq.q: What do I need to run it?
faq.a: A Mac running macOS 27 or later.
No. It saves a .pkpasstemplate bundle. You sign and build the pass with Apple's Pass Builder package or manually, using an Apple-issued certificate from your developer account.

faq.q: Which pass types does it support?
faq.a: Six: boarding pass (air, train, boat, bus or generic), coupon, generic, store card, event ticket and the new poster-style generic pass.

faq.q: Which images does a pass need?
faq.a: PNG files at 2x and 3x; the app tells you which images each pass type needs. Apple's documentation lists sizes such as a 38 by 38 point icon.

faq.q: Where can I see it demonstrated?
faq.a: In Apple's WWDC26 session "What's new in Wallet" (session 209), which covers Pass Designer from 5:47 to 10:40.
